related_questions.question: What is the difference between cor pulmonale and right heart failure?
related_questions.snippet: The definition of cor pulmonale (pulmonary heart) is when a lung issue causes your right ventricle (heart chamber) to get so big that your heart starts to fail. text_blocks.snippet: Cor pulmonale is a condition where the right ventricle of the heart becomes enlarged and weakened due to chronic lung disease. The symptoms of cor pulmonale may include:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath, especially during exertion or at rest
Swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet

text_blocks.snippet: As the condition progresses, symptoms may worsen and additional signs may develop, such as:

list.snippet: Jugular vein distention: (bulging veins in the neck)

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that symptoms of cor pulmonale may vary depending on the underlying lung disease and severity of the condition. If you experience any of these symptoms, it's crucial to seek medical attention promptly for proper diagnosis and treatment.
